title: Uncovering Hidden Nutrient Dynamics in Algal-Bacterial Consortia: Nanoscale Stable Isotope Probing in the Phycosphere
content: The interplay between algae and bacteria in the phycosphere is a critical yet poorly understood driver of nutrient cycling in aquatic ecosystems. Microbial communities associated with algae influence the transformation and assimilation of organic and inorganic nutrients, with implications for algal bloom dynamics, primary production, and biogeochemical cycling. In this study, we employed nanoscale stable isotope probing (nanoSIP) using high-resolution imaging with secondary ion mass spectrometry (nanoSIMS) and metagenomics to elucidate the pathways of organic nitrogen (N) processing within algal-bacterial consortia, focusing on Microcystis, a bloom-forming cyanobacterium. We presented new sights into how microbial consortia mediate nitrogen fluxes and their role in sustaining harmful algal blooms.
